failedApproaches: Approach: run corepack enable in non-admin PowerShell → Result: EPERM on C:\Program Files\nodejs\pnpm → Lesson: Windows requires PowerShell admin for Corepack writes
Approach: run gh auth login in terminal opened before gh install → Result: CommandNotFoundException → Lesson: Windows PATH is frozen per-process, new terminal needed after winget install
Approach: run pnpm db:migrate:deploy with env only in .env.local → Result: P1012 DIRECT_URL not found → Lesson: Prisma CLI reads .env by default, not .env.local; need both files
modifiedFiles: frontend/.env.local: created from .env.example, filled DATABASE_URL (Neon pooled with pgbouncer=true&connection_limit=1&pool_timeout=15), DIRECT_URL (Neon direct), JWT_SECRET (48B base64), CRON_SECRET (32B base64), ENCRYPTION_KEY (32B base64)
frontend/.env: duplicate of .env.local so Prisma CLI picks up DIRECT_URL
Neon DB neondb: 5 Prisma migrations applied (schema public populated with User/Order/Withdrawal/Organization/AdminAction/OAuthAccount + related)
implicitRules: Tech stack: Next.js 16 App Router monolith, Prisma 5 (version 5.22, upgrade to 8 available), pnpm workspace, Neon Postgres with -pooler hostname for app + direct hostname for migrations
Env file convention: frontend/.env.local for Next.js runtime, duplicate frontend/.env for Prisma CLI; both gitignored at root level
Required env vars at boot: DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL, JWT_SECRET (≥32 chars, non-weak), CRON_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY (AES-256-GCM key, 32B base64)
